text:
Carla M: Pushing a short RFC follow-up — proposal for a small proxy service that does rate apportionment at the edge before requests hit the admission layer. Goal: simpler fairness across routes without touching the central quota DB for every request.

Sanjay P: Sketch please. is this per-region? per-pod? :thinking_face:

Carla M: Per-region proxies, sticky to an API gateway node. They only hold soft-state leases (short lived, 1-2s) and request portions for tenants. If a proxy runs out of local capacity it asks central apportioner async and falls back to degraded fairness.

Lee: Why not keep it stateless and ask central each time? complexity tradeoffs?

Carla M: Central on every request costs P95 latency. The apportionment proxy is a local coordinator: for fast-path we do local allocation from recent token buckets aggregated per-tenant+route. Central is source-of-truth for refills and long windows.

Mae: How do we prevent split-brain where two proxies both think they have tokens?

Carla M: Use monotonic lease ids + short lease TTLs. Flow: proxy requests lease window from central: central returns {lease_id, allowed_units, expiry_ts}. Proxy hands out up to allowed_units across N requests and decrements locally. If expiry hits, central can reissue. On conflicts central uses lease_id order to reconcile.

David H: Sounds stateful. where do we persist metrics/usage for billing? we still need accurate accounting.

Carla M: Accounting is append-only events to the central metrics pipeline. Proxies emit usage events (batched every 500ms) with lease_id. Central consumes and reconciles. This gives eventual-correctness for billing while keeping fast-path latency.

Lee: What about abuse — a tenant fires many short-lived connections across proxies to drain distributed buckets?

Carla M: We add abuse detectors at two levels: 1) proxy-local heuristics (rate of new connection IDs, abnormal per-connection tokens) that temporarily reduce local allotment; 2) central anomaly detector that flags tenants and flips to strict central-only allotment or probation windows.

Sanjay P: API contract suggestion for proxy-central interaction? I mocked one: 

```
POST /v1/apportion/lease
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {'tenant_id':'t-123','route':'/generate','desired_units':500,'latency_hint':'p50'}
Response: {'lease_id':'L-456','allowed_units':400,'expiry_unix':1709512400,'policy':'best-effort'}
```

Mae: Add a 'fallback_policy' enum: {best-effort, block, redirect-to-central}. proxies can surface that to gateway to decide HTTP 429 vs queued response.

Carla M: Good call. Also need metrics: lease_granted_count, lease_rejected_count, local_consumed_units, central_reconciled_units, abuse_triggers. All tagged by tenant, route, region.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist: add feature-flag (edge.apportioning.v1), circuit-breaker thresholds, observability dashboards, e2e test harness.

David H: Rollout plan idea: start with low-risk read-only tenants, run in shadow mode (proxies calculate but do not enforce), then opt-in tenants for hard-enforcement 2 weeks later. Canary region -> global.

Lee: One more: backpressure. If central is slow, proxies should gracefully degrade to token-slim mode and surface a header `X-Quota-Proxy: degraded` so callers can adapt.

Carla M: Agreed. I'll write a short follow-up RFC doc with sequence diagrams and the API proto. For now, action items: 
- Carla: draft RFC with sequence diagrams (this week)
- Sanjay: prototype lease proto and bench basic latency (next week)
- Mae: abuse-detector heuristics doc (end of sprint)
- David: billing reconciliation sweeps and test plan

Sanjay P: ack. will also add explicit tests for cross-proxy exhaustion scenarios.

Carla M: thanks all. ping me if you want to pair on the diagram. :thumbsup:
